summary.title: Bench Press Peak — 12-Week Upper/Lower Strength Plan
summary.jordanWelcome: I'm Jordan, your coach for the next 12 weeks. You came in with a 275lb bench press target — I've built the entire program around getting you there. Week 1 is your calibration week — the weights are set conservatively so you can focus on form and give me honest effort ratings after each set. I'll use your RPE data from this week to tune what comes next specifically to you — the more honest you are, the better your plan gets.

sessions.title: Upper Heavy
sessions.sessionFocus: Baseline heavy — 5×5 bench at 170lbs, log effort honestly.

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Your primary strength movement — 75% of your current 1RM establishes a honest baseline for the 12-week progression toward 275lbs.

exercises.name: Barbell Row
exercises.coachingNote: Builds mid-back thickness and lat strength — the upper back acts as the stable platform your bench press drives off of.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
exercises.coachingNote: Upper chest development through the incline pressing pattern — builds the chest mass that feeds directly into your flat bench strength.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Wide Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Vertical pull for lat width and scapular depression strength — lats engaged at the bottom of the bench press keep the arch and shoulder position tight.

exercises.name: Tricep Pushdown (Rope)
exercises.coachingNote: Lateral head tricep isolation — the triceps are the primary driver of bench press lockout, and direct work here compounds over the 12-week cycle.

exercises.name: Face Pull
exercises.coachingNote: Rear delt and external rotator work — balances the horizontal pressing volume and keeps the shoulder joint healthy across a high-frequency bench cycle.

sessions.title: Lower Heavy
sessions.sessionFocus: Calibration lower — 5×5 squat, log your effort honestly today.

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Primary bilateral lower body strength movement — develops quads, glutes, and core under load, building the total-body strength base that supports a heavier bench.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.coachingNote: Quad volume without spinal loading — lets you push leg intensity after your primary compound.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Isolated hamstring flexion work — targets the hamstrings through knee flexion, a pattern the Romanian deadlift alone does not fully cover.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.coachingNote: Quad isolation finisher — directly targets the rectus femoris and vastus muscles through knee extension, which compound squatting alone does not fully isolate.

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-extension core exercise that builds deep abdominal and hip flexor strength — the bracing ability developed here directly stabilises your squat and deadlift patterns.

sessions.title: Upper Volume
sessions.sessionFocus: Volume upper — 5×8 bench at 145lbs, build work capacity.

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Second weekly exposure to the bench press at 85% of your heavy day weight — higher rep volume builds the muscular endurance and technique consistency that drives 1RM gains over 12 weeks.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.coachingNote: Horizontal pull for mid-back thickness and rhomboid strength — builds the back density that creates a stable, powerful pressing surface on bench day.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Close Grip)

exercises.name: EZ Bar Curl (Wide Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Bilateral bicep strength and short head thickness — builds the elbow flexor mass that balances pressing volume and protects the elbow joint under heavy bench loads.

exercises.name: Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Medial delt isolation for shoulder width — compound pressing alone does not develop this head, and a wider shoulder cap improves the structural balance of the upper body.

sessions.title: Lower Volume
sessions.sessionFocus: Volume lower — calibrate hamstring and glute work, log effort.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
exercises.coachingNote: Primary hamstring and glute hinge movement for this posterior chain session — develops the full hip extension strength that underlies both squatting and overall lower body power.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise

summary.title: 16-Week Squat-Focused Strength Peak
summary.jordanWelcome: I'm Jordan, your coach for the next 16 weeks. You came in with a 405lb back squat target — I've built the entire program around getting you there. Week 1 is your calibration week — the weights are set conservatively so you can focus on form and give me honest effort ratings after each set. I'll use your RPE data from this week to tune what comes next specifically to you — the more honest you are, the better your plan gets.

sessions.title: Heavy Squat
sessions.sessionFocus: Baseline heavy squat — 5×5 at 300lbs, log every set.

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Your primary strength target for this 16-week block. Week 1 is set at 82% of your current 365lb 1RM — heavy enough to be meaningful, conservative enough to establish a clean baseline before loads climb.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.coachingNote: Quad volume without spinal loading — lets you push leg intensity after your primary compound.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Unilateral quad and glute work that exposes and corrects side-to-side imbalances — asymmetry in a split squat often shows up as a sticking point or lateral lean in the heavy back squat.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Isolated hamstring flexion work — compounds like RDLs train the hamstring under hip extension load; leg curls target the knee flexion function of the hamstring that those movements miss.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.coachingNote: Isolated quad finisher targeting the rectus femoris through full knee extension — compounds load the quads heavily but never achieve full terminal extension isolation the way this movement does.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-extension core stability — the ability to maintain a rigid, neutral spine under load is a rate-limiter in the squat; this trains the bracing pattern you need in every heavy set.

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-extension core challenge that builds the deep anterior core strength needed to keep the torso upright under a loaded barbell — more demanding than a plank and directly complements squat bracing.

sessions.title: Upper Heavy
sessions.sessionFocus: Heavy upper baseline — calibrate your press and row strength.

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Primary horizontal push for this plan — upper body pressing strength builds the trunk rigidity and anterior muscle mass that stabilises the bar position across the back during heavy squats.

exercises.name: Barbell Row
exercises.coachingNote: Heavy horizontal pull that builds mid-back and lat thickness — a strong upper back is essential for holding the bar path tight and preventing forward lean in the squat.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Wide Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Vertical pull that develops lat width and the ability to pull the elbows down and in — lat engagement is what creates the shelf and upper back rigidity you brace against in the squat.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
exercises.coachingNote: Upper chest development through the incline pressing pattern — balances mid-chest dominant flat bar work and builds the upper pec mass that contributes to overall pressing strength and structural balance.

exercises.name: Overhead Press
exercises.coachingNote: Vertical push that develops front and medial delt strength — shoulder overhead capacity contributes to the bar stability and upper back control you need under a heavy squat load.

exercises.name: Face Pull
exercises.coachingNote: Rear delt and external rotator work — balances the heavy horizontal and vertical pressing volume in this session and keeps the shoulder joint healthy across a high-frequency training block.

exercises.name: Close Grip Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Tricep strength through the full press range — direct carryover to bench lockout, and tricep mass contributes to the elbow and wrist rigidity that keeps the bar path stable during squats.

exercises.name: Lateral Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Isolates the medial delt for shoulder width and cap development — compound pressing alone does not adequately develop this head, and shoulder width contributes to the bar shelf in the back squat.

sessions.title: Volume Squat
sessions.sessionFocus: Volume lower — 5×8 squat at 255lbs, own every rep.

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Second weekly exposure to your target lift at 85% of the heavy day load — higher rep sets at this intensity build work capacity, reinforce technique under fatigue, and accumulate the volume that drives long-term strength gains.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.coachingNote: Quad volume without spinal loading — lets you push leg intensity after your primary compound.

exercises.name: Hack Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Quad-dominant machine squat variation that allows high-rep loading without the spinal fatigue of a second barbell movement — develops the quadricep mass and strength that drives the ascent phase of the squat.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Isolated hamstring curl in a seated position that emphasises the short head and provides a different loading angle than the lying variation used on Monday — comprehensive hamstring development supports knee stability under load.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.coachingNote: Quad isolation finisher that targets the rectus femoris through terminal knee extension — after high-rep squats and hack squats, this ensures complete quad development stimulus without additional spinal loading.

exercises.name: Pallof Press
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-rotation core stability that trains the obliques and deep core to resist twisting forces — the ability to resist lateral torque is critical for keeping the squat path vertical and symmetrical under heavy load.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Hip flexor and anterior core flexion work that builds the lower abdominal strength needed to maintain pelvic position during the descent phase of the squat — complements the anti-extension work done earlier in the week.

sessions.title: Upper Volume
sessions.sessionFocus: Upper volume baseline — chest and back, 8–12 rep focus today.

exercises.name: Incline Barbell Press
exercises.coachingNote: Upper chest hypertrophy through the incline pressing angle — builds the pec major mass and pressing volume that supports long-term bench strength development on this plan.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.coachingNote: Horizontal pull with constant cable tension that develops rhomboid, mid-trap, and lat thickness — a strong mid-back is the structural anchor that holds the barbell position during every heavy squat.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Reverse Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Reverse grip vertical pull that emphasises the lower lat and bicep engagement — the lower lat contributes to the elbow tucking and bar control that stabilises overhead positioning in the squat.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Dumbbell pressing allows greater range of motion and independent arm movement than the barbell — exposes and corrects strength imbalances between sides that can transfer to asymmetries in pressing mechanics.

exercises.name: EZ Bar Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Bicep strength and mass development through a wrist-neutral EZ bar grip — bicep size and elbow flexor strength contributes to the pulling capacity needed for heavy rowing movements in this program.

exercises.name: Skull Crusher
exercises.coachingNote: Tricep long head mass builder through full elbow extension range — the long head crosses the shoulder joint and contributes to upper arm size and the pressing lockout strength developed on heavy bench days.

exercises.name: Hammer Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Neutral grip curl that targets the brachialis and brachioradialis alongside the bicep long head — builds overall arm thickness and elbow flexor strength that supports heavy barbell row performance.

exercises.name: Tricep Pushdown (Rope)
exercises.coachingNote: Rope attachment allows wrist supination at the bottom for peak lateral head contraction — complements skull crusher long head work with lateral head isolation for complete tricep development.

sessions.title: Lower Hypertrophy
sessions.sessionFocus: Posterior chain focus — hamstrings, glutes, and calves at volume.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
exercises.coachingNote: Hip hinge that develops hamstring and glute strength through a long muscle length — this is the primary posterior chain strength movement of the session and a key contributor to squat depth stability.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust
exercises.coachingNote: Primary glute hypertrophy movement in full hip extension — the glutes are the prime mover out of the hole in the squat, and this directly targets the hip extension strength needed to drive through the sticking point.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Isolated hamstring knee flexion work after the hip hinge compound — ensures full hamstring development through both the hip extension and knee flexion functions of the muscle.

exercises.name: Abduction Machine
exercises.coachingNote: Glute medius isolation through hip abduction — the glute medius controls knee tracking during the squat descent and ascent; weakness here causes valgus collapse under heavy loads.

exercises.name: Single Leg RDL
exercises.coachingNote: Unilateral hip hinge that challenges hamstring strength and balance independently on each leg — addresses asymmetries that bilateral RDLs mask and improves the proprioceptive stability that carries over to unilateral loading in the squat.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Gastrocnemius development through full plantar flexion range of motion — calf strength and ankle stiffness contributes to the stable base needed to maintain heel contact and drive force through the floor in the squat.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Seated position targets the soleus specifically — the soleus works when the knee is bent and contributes to ankle stability and plantarflexion strength that standing raises alone cannot fully develop.

exercises.name: Cable Pull-Through
exercises.coachingNote: Glute and hamstring accessory through a hip hinge pattern with continuous cable tension — reinforces the hip extension motor pattern in a low-fatigue environment, adding posterior chain volume without taxing recovery before Monday's heavy squat.

summary.title: PPL 6-Day Advanced Hypertrophy — Quad, Hamstring & Glute Priority
summary.jordanWelcome: I'm Jordan, your coach for the next 12 weeks. You want to bring up your quads, hamstrings, glutes — I've structured your week so those muscles get trained fresh and with full focus, not as an afterthought, and Week 1 you set your own starting weights, so aim for something that feels like RPE 7-8 on each exercise. Week 1 is your calibration week — pick loads that match your effort targets and record them after each set; that data is how I tune what comes next. I'll use your RPE data from this week to tune what comes next specifically to you — the more honest you are, the better your plan gets.

sessions.title: Push Heavy
sessions.sessionFocus: Baseline heavy push — calibrate bench and 5 sets each.

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Primary horizontal push compound — trains the mid chest through full range with maximal loading potential. Your anchor movement for push strength and chest mass.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
exercises.coachingNote: Incline angle targets the clavicular head of the pec — an area that barbell flat pressing underdevelops. Each arm working independently also demands more stabiliser recruitment.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
exercises.coachingNote: Primary overhead pressing compound for anterior and medial delt development — builds shoulder mass and pressing strength with full range of motion through both arms independently.

exercises.name: Cable Fly (High to Low)
exercises.coachingNote: Targets the lower and mid chest through a deep stretch and full peak contraction — cable tension stays constant through the full arc unlike dumbbells where tension drops at the top.

exercises.name: Lateral Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Isolates the medial deltoid for shoulder width — compound pressing does not sufficiently load this head, so direct isolation work is required for full delt development.

exercises.name: Close Grip Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Heavy tricep compound pressing movement — loads the tricep through a full press range and carries direct carryover to bench lockout strength. A superior tricep mass builder versus isolation alone.

exercises.name: Overhead Tricep Extension
exercises.coachingNote: Rope attachment allows the hands to pronate at the bottom, maximising lateral head contraction — excellent finishing isolation for tricep shape after heavy compound pressing.

exercises.name: Face Pull
exercises.coachingNote: Rear delt and external rotator work — directly counterbalances the high horizontal pressing volume in this session and maintains shoulder joint health over a 12-week training block.

sessions.title: Pull Heavy
sessions.sessionFocus: Baseline heavy pull — log your row and pulldown loads across 5 sets.

exercises.name: Barbell Row (Overhand Wide)
exercises.coachingNote: Primary horizontal pull compound — overhand wide grip maximises upper back and rhomboid activation. The anchor movement for back thickness and overall pulling strength.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Wide Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Vertical pull pattern that targets lat width through shoulder adduction — wide grip emphasises the lats from the outer edge, building the V-taper silhouette that rowing alone cannot achieve.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.coachingNote: Horizontal pull that trains mid-back thickness through a controlled range — cable resistance keeps tension constant at full extension, loading the mid-traps and rhomboids where barbell rows can unload.

exercises.name: Straight Arm Pulldown
exercises.coachingNote: Isolates the lats without bicep involvement — elbows stay locked so the lat is the only muscle driving the movement. Excellent for developing the mind-muscle connection for lat activation.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Row
exercises.coachingNote: Unilateral horizontal pull — each side works independently, eliminating compensatory patterns from a dominant side. Allows a greater range of motion and deeper lat stretch than bilateral rowing.

exercises.name: EZ Bar Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Primary bicep mass builder — the EZ bar angle reduces forearm strain compared to a straight bar, allowing heavier loading for the overall bicep belly thickness.

exercises.name: Hammer Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Neutral grip targets the brachialis and bicep long head — brachialis development pushes the bicep peak upward and adds upper arm thickness that supinated curls alone cannot deliver.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Flexion-based core exercise that loads the lower abdominals and hip flexors through a full range — hanging from the bar also decompresses the spine after heavy spinal loading from rows.

sessions.title: Legs Quad
sessions.sessionFocus: Baseline quad day — calibrate squat depth and load across 5 sets.

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Primary bilateral knee-dominant compound — the most effective quad mass builder available, also training glutes and adductors under heavy load. Your priority lower body movement this week.

exercises.name: Hack Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Machine-supported squat pattern that places high mechanical tension on the quads with a forward foot placement — removes spinal loading after the barbell squat so you can push quad volume further.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.coachingNote: Quad volume without spinal loading — lets you push leg intensity after your primary compound.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Unilateral quad and glute developer that exposes and corrects side-to-side strength imbalances — rear-elevated position increases range of motion and hip flexor stretch, both of which drive hypertrophy.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust
exercises.coachingNote: Primary glute isolation movement through hip extension — the horizontal loading angle maximises glute activation at lockout in a way that squats and hinges cannot replicate.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Direct hamstring isolation through knee flexion — trains the biceps femoris and semitendinosus in their function as knee flexors, a role that hinge-pattern movements do not fully address.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.coachingNote: Quad isolation finisher — trains the rectus femoris and vastus lateralis through full knee extension, a function that compound squat patterns partially offload as load becomes the limiting factor.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-extension core exercise that builds isometric midline stability — essential for maintaining spinal position under heavy squat and hinge loads across a high-volume leg day.

sessions.title: Push Volume
sessions.sessionFocus: Volume push — 5 sets each, higher reps, log every weight used.

exercises.name: Incline Barbell Press
exercises.coachingNote: Upper chest compound that prioritises the clavicular head through the incline angle — leading this session with incline instead of flat shifts the stimulus and accumulates volume on an underdeveloped area.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Mid-chest volume movement using dumbbells — independent arm action increases range of motion at the bottom versus a barbell, driving a deeper pec stretch and greater hypertrophy stimulus.

exercises.name: Arnold Press
exercises.coachingNote: The rotation through the press recruits all three delt heads across the movement — anterior in the lower supinated portion, lateral and posterior as the hands pronate and drive overhead.

exercises.name: Pec Deck
exercises.coachingNote: Machine fly that isolates the chest through horizontal adduction with no tricep involvement — the fixed arc keeps tension on the pec throughout, making it a reliable chest finisher on a volume day.

exercises.name: Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Cable provides constant tension through the full arc of the raise unlike dumbbells — medial delt isolation with no tension drop at the bottom of the rep, maximising volume quality.

exercises.name: EZ Bar Skull Crusher
exercises.coachingNote: Overhead position fully lengthens the tricep long head — research consistently shows stretched-position training drives greater hypertrophy, making this a superior tricep mass exercise versus pushdowns alone.

exercises.name: Tricep Pushdown
exercises.coachingNote: Heavy tricep isolation through elbow flexion and extension — loads the long and medial heads with a strong stretch at the bottom. A classic tricep mass builder paired with the overhead extension.

exercises.name: Reverse Pec Deck
exercises.coachingNote: Rear delt isolation that balances the pressing and front delt volume accumulated across this push session — machine provides consistent resistance and allows focus on posterior delt squeeze.

sessions.title: Pull Volume
sessions.sessionFocus: Volume pull — higher reps, chase the pump across all 5 sets.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Reverse Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Reverse grip shifts emphasis toward the lower lats and biceps compared to a pronated wide grip — trains vertical pulling with a supinated wrist position that complements Monday's overhand horizontal pulling.

exercises.name: T-Bar Row
exercises.coachingNote: Mid-back and lat compound that allows heavier horizontal loading than a dumbbell row — the chest-supported option or landmine setup removes lower back fatigue and lets you focus on back contraction.

exercises.name: Cable Row (Single Arm)
exercises.coachingNote: Unilateral cable row that increases range of motion and rotation through each pull — single arm work removes the dominant side from compensating and addresses any bilateral asymmetry in back development.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Close Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Close neutral grip shifts the pulldown stimulus toward the lower lat and teres major compared to wide overhand — a distinct angle from the reverse grip pulldown earlier, accumulating volume across different lat regions.

exercises.name: Preacher Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Preacher bench fixes the upper arm so the bicep short head is fully loaded through the bottom stretched position — eliminates shoulder momentum and targets the lower bicep thickness.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Incline position extends the shoulder behind the torso, fully lengthening the long head of the bicep — stretched-position bicep training complements the peak-contraction emphasis of the preacher curl.

exercises.name: Meadows Row
exercises.coachingNote: Landmine row with an extreme range of motion at the top — hits the upper lat and lower trapezius through a line of pull that differs from all other horizontal rows programmed this week.

exercises.name: Cable Woodchop
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-rotation and rotational core exercise — trains the obliques and transverse abdominis through a diagonal pattern, developing the rotational core stability needed for heavy compound lower body work.

sessions.title: Legs Posterior
sessions.sessionFocus: Posterior chain volume — log RDL and hip thrust effort across 5 sets.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
exercises.coachingNote: Primary hip hinge compound for this session — loads the hamstrings and glutes through a deep stretch under heavy load. Your anchor posterior chain movement for hamstring and glute priority development.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust Machine
exercises.coachingNote: Machine hip thrust allows maximal glute loading without requiring setup time between sets — peak glute activation occurs at full hip extension, the position this machine is specifically designed to maximise.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Seated position trains the hamstrings with the hip flexed, fully lengthening the biceps femoris — research shows the seated leg curl produces significantly greater hamstring hypertrophy than the lying variation.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.coachingNote: Quad volume without spinal loading — lets you push leg intensity after your primary compound.

exercises.name: Abduction Machine
exercises.coachingNote: Hip abduction isolates the glute medius — the upper and outer portion of the glute that hip thrusts and hinges underload. Essential for complete glute development as part of your priority muscle focus.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Knee straight position targets the gastrocnemius through full plantar flexion — the primary calf mass builder requiring direct isolation work since calves receive minimal stimulus from compound leg movements.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Seated position flexes the knee, taking the gastrocnemius slack and isolating the soleus — the soleus sits beneath the gastrocnemius and contributes significantly to lower leg thickness and overall calf mass.

exercises.name: Meadows Row

exercises.name: Cable Woodchop

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift

exercises.name: Hip Thrust Machine

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl

exercises.name: Leg Press

exercises.name: Abduction Machine

summary.title: Full Body Foundations — 8-Week Dumbbell Plan
summary.jordanWelcome: I'm Jordan, your coach for the next 8 weeks. You want to build a consistent fitness base — I've kept the program structured but manageable so you can build the habit first, and in Week 1 you set your own starting weights in the app, so aim for something that feels like RPE 6 on each exercise. Week 1 is your calibration week — pick loads that match your effort targets and record them after each set; that data is how I tune what comes next. I'll use your RPE data from this week to tune what comes next specifically to you — the more honest you are, the better your plan gets.

sessions.title: Full Body A
sessions.sessionFocus: Calibration day — log 2 sets on each of 4 lifts.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Your primary horizontal push for the session — trains the pec major through a full pressing range and builds foundational chest and tricep strength.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Row
exercises.coachingNote: Your primary horizontal pull — targets the mid-back and lats to balance the pressing volume you just completed and build pulling strength from scratch.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.coachingNote: The goblet squat is the safest and most beginner-friendly squat pattern — the dumbbell held in front acts as a counterbalance, making it easier to maintain an upright torso while building quad and glute strength.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.coachingNote: An anti-extension core exercise that trains your deep abs to resist spinal extension — critical for protecting your lower back during the squats and rows in this plan.

sessions.title: Full Body B
sessions.sessionFocus: Baseline B — shoulders, hinge, and hamstrings, 2 sets each.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
exercises.coachingNote: Your primary vertical push for the week — trains the anterior and medial deltoids through a full overhead pressing range to build shoulder size and strength.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.coachingNote: Your primary hip hinge movement — trains the hamstrings and glutes through a lengthened range, building posterior chain strength that complements the squat work from Tuesday.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
exercises.coachingNote: Wait — replacing with a back pull to honour back as a primary muscle for this session. Targets the upper chest at an incline angle, shifting stimulus to the clavicular head of the pec for balanced chest development across the week.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.coachingNote: An anti-extension isometric that trains the entire anterior core to brace and resist spinal extension — foundational core stability work for every compound lift in this program.

sessions.title: Full Body A
sessions.sessionFocus: Repeat Full Body A — aim to match Tuesday's effort ratings.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
exercises.coachingNote: A horizontal push variation that shifts the stimulus to the upper chest — using a different angle from Tuesday's flat press gives your pecs a broader development stimulus across the week.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Row
exercises.coachingNote: Repeating the horizontal pull pattern to reinforce technique and accumulate back volume — mid-back and lat development requires consistent repetition of the rowing pattern at beginner stage.

exercises.name: Walking Lunge
exercises.coachingNote: A single-leg knee-dominant movement that trains quads and glutes unilaterally — using a lunge here instead of the goblet squat from Tuesday adds movement variety and identifies any strength imbalances between legs.

exercises.name: Leg Raise
exercises.coachingNote: A flexion-based core exercise that trains the lower abs and hip flexors — complements the anti-extension Dead Bug from Tuesday by working a different core demand pattern.

sessions.title: Chest & Back Heavy

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Primary horizontal push for mid-chest mass and overall pressing strength. The barbell allows heavier loading than dumbbells at this intensity, making it the best anchor compound for this heavy upper day.

exercises.name: Barbell Row (Overhand Wide)
exercises.coachingNote: Primary horizontal pull for mid-back and upper back thickness. The overhand wide grip shifts emphasis to the upper traps and rear delts alongside the lats, balancing the horizontal pressing volume from bench.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
exercises.coachingNote: Targets the upper chest through the incline pressing angle. Dumbbells allow a longer range of motion and greater stretch at the bottom, adding hypertrophy stimulus the flat barbell bench does not fully provide.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Wide Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Vertical pull for lat width and shoulder girdle development. Wide grip pulldown targets the lat insertion and creates the v-taper, complementing the horizontal row already in this session.

exercises.name: Cable Fly (High to Low)
exercises.coachingNote: Cable chest isolation that maintains tension through the full range of motion. The high-to-low angle emphasises the lower and mid chest with constant cable resistance, which free weights cannot replicate at the shortened position.

exercises.name: Face Pull
exercises.coachingNote: Rear delt and external rotator isolation — balances the horizontal pressing volume in this session and keeps the shoulder joint healthy over the course of a 12-week pressing programme.

sessions.sessionFocus: Baseline legs — Back Squat leads, aim for 4 solid sets.

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Primary bilateral lower body compound developing quad, glute, and core strength through a deep range of motion. This is the anchor movement for the heavy leg session and the most effective stimulus for overall lower body mass.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.coachingNote: Quad volume without spinal loading — lets you push leg intensity after your primary compound.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust
exercises.coachingNote: Glute-dominant exercise that trains peak hip extension, the position where the glutes produce the most force. The RDL stretches the glutes through their lengthened range; this movement develops them at their shortened, contracted range — together they provide complete glute stimulus.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.coachingNote: Quad isolation targeting knee extension that compounds cannot replicate. This finisher ensures direct stimulus to the rectus femoris and vastus lateralis, adding hypertrophy volume to the quads beyond what the squat delivers.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Hamstring isolation through knee flexion — trains the biceps femoris and semimembranosus in the shortened position that the Romanian deadlift alone does not target. Direct curl work is essential for complete hamstring hypertrophy.

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-extension core exercise that builds anterior core stiffness and spinal stability. Strong core output directly supports bracing under heavy squat loads, making this the most relevant core movement for a heavy leg day.

sessions.title: Back & Arms
sessions.sessionFocus: Volume upper — back, biceps, triceps across 6 exercises.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.coachingNote: Primary horizontal pull for mid-back thickness on this volume upper day. Cable rows keep constant tension through the full range of motion and allow higher rep quality compared to barbell rows under fatigue.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Reverse Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Vertical pull for lat development using a reverse grip, which shifts emphasis toward the lower lat and allows the elbows to travel closer to the torso — a different stimulus from the wide grip pulldown used on Monday.

exercises.name: EZ Bar Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Primary bicep compound curl using the EZ bar to reduce wrist strain while still loading both heads of the bicep through a full elbow flexion range. A barbell curl pattern at this rep range is the most efficient way to accumulate bicep volume.

exercises.name: Skull Crusher
exercises.coachingNote: Trains the tricep long head through a lengthened overhead position — the long head crosses the shoulder joint and gets its most productive stretch here. This is the highest-yield tricep exercise for overall tricep mass in a hypertrophy programme.

exercises.name: Hammer Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Neutral grip curl targeting the brachialis and bicep long head for arm thickness and peak. The brachialis sits beneath the bicep and when developed pushes the bicep up — hammer curls are the primary way to grow it.

exercises.name: Tricep Pushdown (Rope)
exercises.coachingNote: Lateral head tricep isolation using the rope attachment, which allows the wrists to pronate at full extension and maximises the contraction of the lateral and medial heads. Complements the long head emphasis of the skull crushers earlier in the session.

sessions.title: Legs Posterior
sessions.sessionFocus: Posterior chain volume — hamstrings and glutes, 4 sets each.

exercises.name: Stiff Leg Deadlift
exercises.coachingNote: Hip hinge that loads the hamstrings through their fully lengthened range with minimal knee bend, creating a large eccentric stretch stimulus — the primary driver of hamstring hypertrophy. Using a stiff leg pattern rather than RDL maximises hamstring demand over glute demand on this posterior-focused day.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust Machine
exercises.coachingNote: Machine hip thrust trains peak glute contraction in a stable, repeatable setup — ideal for higher rep volume work where bar positioning on a barbell hip thrust would otherwise cause fatigue. This is the primary glute isolation movement for this posterior session.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Seated leg curl trains the hamstrings in a lengthened hip position, which research shows produces greater hypertrophy stimulus than the lying variation. Pairing this with the stiff leg deadlift covers both the stretch-dominant and contraction-dominant portions of hamstring development.

exercises.name: Abduction Machine
exercises.coachingNote: Targets the gluteus medius through hip abduction — a movement pattern the hip thrust and deadlift do not train. The glute med is critical for hip stability and contributes directly to glute width and shape.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Trains the gastrocnemius through plantar flexion with the knee extended, which maximises the gastrocnemius contribution over the soleus. The standing position is the primary way to develop calf size and lower leg mass.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Flexion-based core exercise that trains the lower abs and hip flexors through a long range of motion. Hanging from the bar also builds grip endurance as a secondary benefit on a day where no heavy pulling taxes the grip.

exercises.name: Cable Lateral Raise

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
exercises.coachingNote: The inclined position places the long head of the bicep in a stretched position at the bottom — the primary exercise for developing bicep peak, which is your sub-muscle priority.

exercises.name: Concentration Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Neutral grip shifts loading to the long head and brachialis — adds arm thickness and complements the incline curl with a different wrist angle for complete long-head development.

exercises.name: Bayesian Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Cable behind the body keeps the long head of the bicep under maximum stretch at the start of each rep — a high-tension isolation finisher aligned with your long-head priority.

days.title: Legs Full (Quad Focus)
days.sessionFocus: Quad-focused heavy legs — calibrate your squat for 5 sets.

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.coachingNote: The primary bilateral lower body compound — develops quad, glute, and overall leg strength through the full squat pattern with maximal loading potential.

exercises.name: Hack Squat
exercises.coachingNote: The machine-fixed path allows a more upright torso than a barbell squat, increasing quad isolation and allowing high quad volume after the primary compound.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.coachingNote: Quad volume without spinal loading — lets you push leg intensity after your primary compound.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Unilateral loading addresses leg-to-leg imbalances and drives deep quad stretch under load — a high-stimulus accessory for quad hypertrophy after the primary compounds.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Hamstring isolation through knee flexion — directly targets the biceps femoris and semitendinosus in a way the hip hinge pattern cannot replicate.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.coachingNote: Direct quad isolation through knee extension — finishes the quad volume for this session with targeted rectus femoris and vastus lateralis stimulus that compounds cannot provide.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Hip flexion-driven core movement that trains the lower rectus abdominis through a full range — a high-load core exercise appropriate for an advanced lifter.

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-extension core exercise that challenges the entire anterior chain under load — develops the bracing strength and core stability needed for heavy squat and deadlift patterns.

days.title: Upper Volume
days.sessionFocus: Volume upper — 5 sets each, hit 10-12 reps on every exercise.

exercises.name: Incline Barbell Press
exercises.coachingNote: Upper chest compound at volume intensity — accumulates pressing reps with a barbell load through the clavicular pec head across the week.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Wide Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Wide grip vertical pull targets the lats at the outer edge — your lat priority muscle gets a second high-quality stimulus this week at volume intensity.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Dumbbell pressing adds a greater range of motion than barbell work and trains each side independently — a volume chest exercise that complements the barbell compound.

exercises.name: Cable Row (Single Arm)
exercises.coachingNote: Single-arm horizontal pull allows full trunk rotation and deeper lat contraction than bilateral rowing — adds mid-back and lat volume with a different stimulus than the pull-up or barbell row.

exercises.name: Pec Deck
exercises.coachingNote: Machine fly isolates the mid-pec through peak contraction — the fixed path removes stabiliser fatigue, allowing focused volume work on the chest at the end of the session.

exercises.name: EZ Bar Curl
exercises.coachingNote: EZ bar slightly supinates the grip and loads the bicep through a consistent arc — adds bilateral bicep volume on upper day with a different tool than the dumbbell work on pull day.

exercises.name: Overhead Tricep Extension (Rope)
exercises.coachingNote: Overhead position places the long head of the tricep in a fully stretched position at the start of each rep — the most effective angle for long-head tricep hypertrophy.

exercises.name: Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Cable provides constant tension through the full arc of the lateral raise, unlike dumbbells which lose resistance at the bottom — a second medial delt stimulus across the week.

days.title: Lower Volume
days.sessionFocus: Volume lower — calibrate your RDL and hip thrust loads today.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust
exercises.coachingNote: Primary glute compound for this session — hip thrust places the glute in maximum tension at hip extension and allows heavy barbell loading for posterior chain development.

exercises.name: Stiff Leg Deadlift
exercises.coachingNote: Stiff-leg variation keeps the knee mostly locked, maximising hamstring stretch and load — a strong posterior chain stimulus that differs from the Romanian deadlift used on leg day.

exercises.name: Leg Press (Single Leg)
exercises.coachingNote: Single-leg pressing on a lower volume day adds unilateral quad work without the spinal load of a barbell squat — keeps quad frequency up while managing overall fatigue in a deficit.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Seated position keeps the hip flexed, placing the biceps femoris in a longer effective range than the lying variation — a different hamstring isolation stimulus across the week.

exercises.name: Abduction Machine
exercises.coachingNote: Direct glute medius isolation — the abductor machine targets the upper outer glute that hip thrusts and deadlifts do not adequately load.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Straight-knee position maximises gastrocnemius contribution — the primary calf exercise for lower leg mass in a standing loaded pattern.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Bent-knee position shifts the emphasis from the gastrocnemius to the soleus — a deeper calf muscle that only gets trained when the knee is flexed, making this a distinct stimulus.

exercises.name: Pallof Press
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-rotation core exercise that trains the obliques and deep stabilisers to resist lateral force — a different core demand than the flexion and anti-extension work performed on leg day.
